# Evidence behind the skill-testing rules

Every number in this file is **an example from that work**, not a threshold. Part A is read from the records and run results of the CWN2026 course (opened and read by us 2026-11-04). Part B came from an agent searching the web on 2026-11-04 through a tool that has a model summarise the web page first, so the numbers come from summaries, have not been compared with the full page, and differ by paper version.

## Contents
- [A · From real work in the course](#a--from-real-work-in-the-course)
- [B · From research and web documents](#b--from-research-and-web-documents)

## A · From real work in the course

| Topic | What was seen (example from that work) | Rule obtained | Limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| The trigger query set must come from someone who never saw the description | Simulated finding a skill with BM25 (search by words, not Claude choosing a skill), a library of 23 · the "seen" query set of 60 got hit@1 98.3% · the "new" set written by another Claude that never saw the skills got hit@1 80%, hit@5 95% · in the first set 58 of 60 queries had words from the description word for word · the items not found in the top 5 were commands mixing Thai and English (read from the course record 2026-11-04) | The person or agent who writes the trigger test set must never have seen the description · include both Thai and English words that users really type | Measured once, n=60, with BM25, not Claude's own skill choice |
| A red round must also score the process and silent interpretation | The round without the skill passed 39 of 40 tests, but the agent ran `ls petshop` (breaking the black-box rule) and interpreted "อาหารแมว" (cat food) as counting treats without saying so · under the other interpretation the verdict flipped from "can release" to "not yet released" (course record 2026-11-04) | Passing results are not enough to conclude the skill is not the cause · also score whether any step was done wrongly and whether the agent made a decision on its own without telling | Run once, n=1 |
| A skill draft written by AI needs a person to read it before merging | v1, written by AI, chose the interpretation of "อาหารแมว" that made the tests pass, and stayed silent · a person found it in LAB 3, so a rule was added to try the other interpretation and report whether the verdict flips (course record 2026-11-04) | Read the draft looking for where the AI decided on its own to make the tests pass | 1 skill |
| Try the real work 1 round before writing a skill | The course teaches having AI do the real work first, then capturing it as a skill, because a skill should come from a method that worked (source: a clip in the course record) | Do the real work once before drafting | The reasoning is cited from a clip, not measured by comparison |
| A leaking test round | The agent walked into the company rule set, the deal folder and another department's skills in the plugin cache by itself (happened 2 times) · usable results came from rounds run in an empty folder with other plugins hidden (course record 2026-11-04) | Run red/green in an empty folder, hide other plugins, and do not leave the real work folder nearby | Found in a lab where 21 people shared one machine |
| The judge must be blind | Had the judge score 2 versions of a plan without saying which has the skill (A/B labels kept in a separate answer file), 12 criteria written beforehand, result 1/12 (no skill) and 12/12 (with skill) (course run result 2026-11-04) | The judge does not know which version has the skill · swap the A/B labels · write the criteria beforehand | A single pair, the judge was another Claude |
| Written in settings is not the same as installed | The template wrote the name `core` in settings but did not install it · after opening Claude again, counting the skills actually seen gave 13 of 21 desks with no `core` (course record 2026-11-04) | After installing, open a new chat and count the skills the agent really sees | One lab |
| An absolute prohibition should not live only in a skill | The black-box rule was in a skill · when asked about the plan without calling the skill, the agent opened the whole plan file including the answer section (course record 2026-11-04) | A "never" rule that cannot be missed goes in a hook or CLAUDE.md too (our own conclusion; the course record advises stating the rule yourself or calling it via a slash command) | 1 case |
| A lesson that is written down needs a scope and an expiry date | The plan owner's earlier answer is valid when the plan name, URL, number of tests and wording in the plan match · if the wording changes, the answer expires · the "expiry" test was reported by Claude itself and the reviewer did not rerun it (course record 2026-11-04) | Tie a lesson to the source wording | Not yet confirmed again |
| Editing plugin content needs a version bump | `claude plugin update` answered that it is already latest, because `plugin.json` was still 1.0.0 although the content in `SKILL.md` had changed, so it had to be uninstalled and reinstalled (course record 2026-11-04) | Raise `version` in `plugin.json` every time the content changes | Our validator does not check this yet (searched `scripts/check` 2026-11-04), so do it by hand |

## B · From research and web documents

Viewed 2026-11-04 through summaries from a web-fetch tool · read the full page before citing further

| Source | What it reports | Meaning for us |
|---|---|---|
| SkillsBench (arXiv 2602.12670 · submitted 2026-02-13 · revised to version 4 on 2026-06-14) | Skills written by people improve the pass rate · skills written by the LLM itself score lower than no skill in all 3 harnesses of version 4 (about −8.1 · −11.3 · −11.5 points) · version 1 reported human-written skills at +16.2 points, and the abstract figure in the course was 33.9 → 50.5 (+16.6 points, 87 tasks) · version 1 itself is inconsistent (86 vs 84 tasks) · 1 skill +18.0 · 2–3 skills +19.0 · 4 or more +10.1 points (preprint, medium confidence) | A draft from an LLM must pass a human reader and an eval before merging · skills should be small, narrow, and few per task · always label each number with its version |
| arXiv 2608.11888 (2026-08-12) | Even a skill that looks relevant can make things worse · 307 failure cases = wrong role 125 + slower or costlier 182 · the cause is redundant steps (repeated checking 67 · heavy pipeline 30) | An eval must report tokens and time per arm, not only pass or fail |
| arXiv 2608.23067 (2026-08-24 · web only · low to medium confidence) | Adding a skill lowers Pass@2 by 1.3–4.2% and raises tokens by 72–394% · anti-pattern style rules beat long examples | The "1 real example" item in section 2 should be measured for whether it is worth the tokens, not deleted |
| agentskills.io optimizing-descriptions and anthropics/skills skill-creator (2 official sources agree) | Measuring trigger: about 20 queries (8–10 should open · 8–10 should not, focusing on near words with different jobs) · 3 rounds per query · passes when the rate > 0.5 · split train 60% / validation 40% · choose the description by validation · at most 5 rounds · count it as opened only when a real Skill tool call is seen | The full method is in [`eval-format`](eval-format.md), section "Making trigger measurement tighter" |
| Claude Code docs (skills · plugin-evals) | Skill content stays in context every turn, so write it as standing instructions · after compaction about 5,000 tokens per skill are kept, 25,000 in total · skill-creator uses `evals/evals.json`, a different format from `claude plugin eval` (neither reads the other's files) · plugin eval needs git 2.31 or later · `tool_used: Skill` passes but delta is negative: suspect the judge first, then rerun with `--judge-model sonnet` · the description per the Agent Skills spec is at most 1,024 characters, and Claude Code cuts at 1,536 | Used as recorded in section 1 and `eval-format` |
